record.nameMeaning: "Chambered lizard", for the hollow chambers in its vertebrae
record.oneLiner: The most common sauropod of the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation.
record.description: Camarasaurus was a bulky sauropod with a proportionally short neck, a large, strongly built skull and powerful jaws bearing spoon-shaped teeth. The most common dinosaur of the Morrison Formation of western North America and one of the best-understood sauropods, it is known from over 530 specimens. It was probably a selective browser feeding 2–5 m off the ground.

notableFacts.text: The most common dinosaur of the Morrison Formation.
Powerful jaws and spoon-shaped teeth suited it to tough plants.
One specimen may have reached about 40 years old — among the oldest ages reported for a dinosaur.
